To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the exposure to styrene at levels higher than 50 ppm in air may affect logical memory and visuo-constructional abilities, and at levels higher than about 25 ppm in air, verbal memory and learning skills.
the intensity of exposure to styrene was related to the scores of neuropsychological tests, and that the exposure-effect relationships were dose dependent.
exposure to styrene is associated with a significant decrease in verbal learning and in logical memory and visuoconstructive abilities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a neuropsychological test-battery to be used as a sensitive tool for detecting neurotoxic effects of styrene in workers exposed to this solvent.
the effects of exposure to styrene on neuropsychological functions, as assessed by means of an extensive test battery, in a group of workers exposed to styren in the boat-building industry.
a quantitative approach to the study of the effects of styrene on human neuropsychological functioning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of styrene exposure are dose dependent.
exposure to styrene at levels of 25-50 ppm (mean daily) for more than 2-3 years can lead to neuropsychological impairments.

exposure to styrene at the current occupational levels does not produce significant neuropsychological effects in workers exposed for a long time (more than 10 years) and with a mean daily exposure of less than 25 ppm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exposure to styrene at levels higher than 50 ppm in air is associated with impairment in verbal memory and visuoconstructive functions.
the exposure to styrene at the level of about 50 ppm in air for more than 6 h/day is associated with a significant impairment of the neuropsychologic functions in the exposed workers.
the exposure to styrene is associated with a dose-dependent impairment of verbal and visuo-constuctive abilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exposure-effect relationship between styrene and the neuropsychological functions can be described by a threshold model, with a threshold value of MA and PGA of 150 mmole creatinine.
styrene exposure is associated with a decrease in the performance of neuropsychological tests in workers, with an impairment of verbal learning and memory and of visuo-constructing skills.
styrene exposure is related to the impairment of neuropsychological skills.
